title: Three Italians Skip Delhi Immigration, Fly to Munich; Air India Gets Notice
excerpt: The passengers landed at Delhi airport at 12:50 am on September 4 and boarded a Lufthansa flight 55 minutes later without immigration checks, prompting a show-cause notice and an emergency Home Ministry meeting.
body:
• Three Italian nationals landed at Delhi's IGI airport at 12:50 am on September 4 on Air India flight AI-1115 from Amritsar and boarded Lufthansa flight LH-763 to Munich at 1:45 am without clearing mandatory departure immigration.
  • The Ministry of Civil Aviation issued a show-cause notice to Air India on September 12, calling the incident a "serious security and immigration-related lapse" and giving the airline seven days to respond.
  • The Home Ministry has called an emergency meeting on Tuesday, September 15, chaired by Home Secretary Govind Mohan, with top officials from aviation, the Intelligence Bureau, the Bureau of Immigration, Air India and Delhi airport.

Three Italian passengers travelled from Amritsar to Delhi on an Air India flight in the early hours of September 4 and boarded a Lufthansa flight to Munich 55 minutes later without completing mandatory immigration formalities — exposing a serious procedural gap at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport and triggering government action against the airline.

"a serious security and immigration-related lapse"

— Ministry of Civil Aviation, in the show-cause notice to Air India

According to LiveMint, the three passengers arrived in Delhi on AI-1115 at 12:50 am and departed for Munich on Lufthansa LH-763 at 1:45 am. At Amritsar, they had been issued a domestic — "D" category — boarding pass for the Amritsar-Delhi sector, along with onward boarding passes for their Lufthansa journey, and after reaching Delhi they were escorted to the international-to-international transfer area instead of being routed through immigration.

Context & Background

The lapse sits inside a new procedural framework. Air India operates a "hub-and-spoke" arrangement — also referred to as "Easy Connect" — on some routes, under which passengers travelling overseas via a hub airport can complete immigration formalities at the origin, or "spoke," airport. Their boarding passes carry an "I" designator, letting airline staff distinguish them from ordinary domestic passengers, according to fact.net.in.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-NChhiVUSHM

But the three Italians' journey was not covered by that arrangement, LatestLY reported. They were therefore required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi airport and complete immigration before proceeding to their Lufthansa flight. Instead, they were directed to the international transfer area, which meant they never reached the immigration counter before boarding the flight to Munich. The ministry has questioned why Air India issued the onward boarding passes at Amritsar when the journey did not qualify for the hub-and-spoke procedure.

Impact & Analysis

The civil aviation ministry's show-cause notice, issued on September 12 after concerns were raised by the Home Ministry, describes the episode as a violation of the approved standard operating procedure governing hub-and-spoke operations and gives Air India seven days to explain why regulatory or administrative action should not be taken. Air India has not commented on the incident, according to LiveMint.

The Home Ministry's response signals how seriously the breach is being taken. Tuesday's emergency meeting at Kartavya Bhawan will be chaired by Home Secretary Govind Mohan and attended by the secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, the Intelligence Bureau director, the secretary and additional secretary of the home ministry, the Bureau of Immigration commissioner, the Air India Group head and the Delhi airport CEO, according to News89 with PTI inputs.

Diaspora Angle

The Amritsar-Delhi route is a lifeline for the Punjabi diaspora, many of whom fly into Amritsar and connect onward through Delhi. The hub-and-spoke system was designed to make those transfers smoother — and this incident puts that very convenience under the microscope, with tighter checks likely to follow for every transit passenger.

What's Next

Air India's seven-day window to respond to the show-cause notice is now ticking, and Tuesday evening's Home Ministry meeting is expected to set the terms for stricter oversight of airline handling of transit passengers. The outcome will decide whether the airline faces regulatory action — and whether the hub-and-spoke SOP gets a rewrite.
